claims.text: By default a Pod is non-isolated for ingress: with no NetworkPolicy selecting it, it accepts connections from any Pod in the cluster, in any namespace.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Concepts > Services, Load Balancing, and Networking > Network Policies ('The two sorts of pod isolation', 'Default policies'); Cluster Networking / networking model

claims.text: Namespaces scope names and API access (RBAC); they do not restrict network traffic between Pods by themselves.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Concepts > Overview > Namespaces; Network Policies (default non-isolated)

claims.text: A Pod is isolated for ingress when any NetworkPolicy selects it with Ingress in policyTypes; then the only allowed connections are those from the Pod's node and those allowed by the ingress list of some policy that applies to it. Reply traffic is implicitly allowed.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Network Policies, 'The two sorts of pod isolation'

claims.text: NetworkPolicies are additive and do not conflict: the allowed connections are the union of what the applicable policies allow, so evaluation order does not matter and no policy can deny what another allows.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Network Policies ('Network policies do not conflict; they are additive')

claims.text: NetworkPolicies are implemented by the network plugin; creating one without a plugin that implements it has no effect, while the API server still accepts the object.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Network Policies, 'Prerequisites' and note under the example

claims.text: kind 0.33's default network plugin, kindnet, enforces NetworkPolicies (ingress); verified on donhang-staging by network-policy.sh output.
claims.source_hint: kind.sigs.k8s.io release notes (kindnet network policy support); outputs/stage-3/scripts/k8s/network-policy.txt; DECISIONS.md repo-stage 3 F1 'kindnet thực thi NetworkPolicy ingress trên staging'

claims.text: pg_isready only checks the connection status of a PostgreSQL server; it prints 'accepting connections' when the server accepts them and 'no response' (exit code 2) when the connection attempt gets no response.
claims.source_hint: postgresql.org: PostgreSQL Client Applications > pg_isready (Description, Exit Status)

claims.text: Kubelet probes come from the Pod's node, and connections from the node are always allowed into an isolated Pod, so default-deny does not make Pods unready. An ordinary Pod on that node uses its own Pod IP, not the node's, and needs a from rule (hostNetwork Pods aside).
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Network Policies (connections from the pod's node allowed); outputs/stage-3/scripts/k8s/network-policy.txt ('Pods in donhang not ready: 0')

claims.text: policyTypes lists the directions a policy applies to (Ingress = incoming to the selected Pods). An empty podSelector {} selects all Pods in the namespace; with policyTypes [Ingress] and no ingress rules it isolates them all and allows no ingress.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Network Policies, 'podSelector' and 'Default deny all ingress traffic'

claims.text: In ingress.from, podSelector selects Pods in the policy's own namespace; namespaceSelector selects all Pods in matching namespaces; each rule allows traffic matching both from and ports.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Network Policies, 'Behavior of to and from selectors', 'ingress'

claims.text: Kubernetes sets the immutable label kubernetes.io/metadata.name=<name> on every namespace.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Reference > Well-Known Labels, Annotations and Taints (kubernetes.io/metadata.name); Namespaces 'Automatic labelling'

network-policy.sh at stage-3: lines 9-22 define reach_db (pg_isready -t 5 from Pod probe) and start probe in security-lessons; lines 24-48 check, commit the file to the config repo, wait for Argo CD sync, check again, curl the api; lines 49-50 count not-ready Pods.
Output: no policies, then 'accepting connections'; after sync 8 policies listed, 'no response' with exit code 2, GET /api/v1/products HTTP 200, 0 Pods not ready.
kubectl run labels the Pod it creates run=<name>; such a Pod in donhang matches no app value in policy db, so pg_isready -h db reports 'no response' even inside the same namespace.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: kubectl run reference (default label run=<name>); Network Policies (podSelector matches labels)
